loads.name: Crew systems, per person
loads.source: NASA TM-105925 (1993) First Lunar Outpost power, p.6 and Table 2: crew of 4, 45-day stay; habitat needs 10 kWe by day and 9 kWe at night; allocation: crew systems 6.0 kWe
loads.notes: 6.0 kWe for 4 crew, so 1.5 kW per person, scaled by crew size. The memo does not itemise crew systems further. Fixed. Runs always

loads.name: Avionics and communications (without the Earth transmitter)
loads.source: NASA TM-105925 (1993) First Lunar Outpost power, p.6 and Table 2: crew of 4, 45-day stay; habitat needs 10 kWe by day and 9 kWe at night; allocation: avionics 1.8 kWe
loads.notes: The memo's 1.8 kWe avionics and communications allocation minus our 300 W Earth transmitter (li_crew_radio), so at a site in constant contact the two add back to the memo's 1.8 kWe. Receiving and short-range radios stay in here. Fixed. Runs always

loads.name: Radio transmitting to Earth
loads.source: Our estimate. RF transmit power 10-100 W in NASA's Earth-to-lunar-surface link trades (Booth & Marsden, NASA/TM-2019-220203, 2019, which varied surface transmit power at 10, 50 and 100 W)
loads.notes: DC draw taken as ~3x the 100 W RF output (an amplifier about a third efficient); low = 100 W (30 W RF at the same efficiency). Runs only while Earth is in direct contact: above the 10 m antenna's skyline and a DSN station can see the Moon. Editable

loads.name: Other habitat systems
loads.source: NASA TM-105925 (1993) First Lunar Outpost power, p.6 and Table 2: crew of 4, 45-day stay; habitat needs 10 kWe by day and 9 kWe at night
loads.notes: The memo's 10 kWe daytime total minus its three listed allocations (6.0 + 1.8 + 1.0 = 8.8 kWe). Includes thermal control and health monitoring. Fixed. Runs always

loads.name: Science lab
loads.source: NASA TM-105925 (1993) First Lunar Outpost power, p.6 and Table 2: crew of 4, 45-day stay; habitat needs 10 kWe by day and 9 kWe at night; allocation: laboratory science experiments 1.0 kWe
loads.notes: Fixed. Daylight only, which is why the memo has 10 kWe by day and 9 kWe at night

extra_loads.name: Small rover charging
extra_loads.source: NASA VIPER rover: 450 W peak solar power (NTRS 20230011558, VIPER mission overview)
extra_loads.notes: Rover peak power, used as its charging draw. Fixed. Daylight only

extra_loads.name: Crewed rover charging
extra_loads.source: NASA TM-105925 (1993) Table 2: crewed rover recharge 1.4 kWe day and night, 14 h per recharge
